correctness.rationale: For positive m the six counts give an undirected looped multigraph and realization is exactly existence of an Euler trail read as a vertex word. On at most three active vertices the even number of odd degrees is zero or two, so connectivity suffices. Removing loops gives a skeleton; each loop count is distributed among that vertex's visits. With distinct endpoints fix the orientation, so nonunique loop placements at a repeated vertex furnish genuinely different reversal classes. All-even nonconstant skeletons can start at different active vertices and reversal preserves that start. A single ordinary edge type gives an alternating skeleton; the odd cases are unique up to reversal, with both visits repeated once the multiplicity is at least three. On a path with both multiplicities at least two and some odd degree, reserve the forced first and/or last leaf edge for each odd multiplicity; the remaining center excursions include both leaf types and can be swapped. A multiplicity-one leaf instead forces an initial edge and then the single alternating sequence through the other leaf, giving precisely the stated loop freedoms at t=1,2 and t>=3. With three ordinary types and odd endpoints A,B, deleting either initial edge AB or AC leaves a connected ordinary graph with the requisite endpoints for the residual trail; hence distinct skeletons. Counting the disjoint loop freedoms as geometric factors verifies both rational series and the U_m coefficient formula. The leading coefficients are 3/2 and 1/120 in degrees two and five, so the ratio is 180/m^3. For m=0 the three one-letter words share one nonsingleton deck. Independent literal word enumeration through m=11 matched each structural test and both counts: 797,160 words, 9,901 profiles and 1,392 singleton profiles across the checked lengths. Scope is linear labeled ternary words, exact length-two unoriented counts, and global reversal; the ratio is not a uniform-word probability. The finite replay corroborates but does not replace the all-length proof.

value.rationale: Three labels give a natural first nonbinary alphabet and the first case with competing leaf excursions and three ordinary edge types. The classification is a direct test of exact profile identifiability from six integers. The rational census, parity correction and polynomial scarcity law quantitatively distinguish this identifiability question from the established realizability count. No claims are made about noisy reads, all fiber sizes, or code performance.
